sentences.text: The petitioners are before this Court calling in question the registration of a crime in Crime No.0084/2023 registered for offences punishable under Sections 498-A, 504 read with Section 34 of the IPC and under Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

2. Heard Sri. Shekhar Badiger, learned counsel appearing for the petitioners, Sri. B.N. Jagadeesha,
learned Addl.SPP appearing for respondent No.1, Smt. Jayashree Patil, learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2 and have perused the material on record.
3.
The parties to the lis were also before the Family Court in M.C.No.3238/2023 and have settled the dispute NC: 2024:KHC:45847 amongst themselves before the Family Court by terms of settlement.
One of the term of the settlement is, closure of the present proceedings.

The said term in the settlement reads as follows:
"MEMORANDUM OF SETTLEMENT UNDER SECTION 89 OF CPC READ WITH RULES 24 AND 25 OF THE KARNATAKA CIVIL PROCEDURE (MEDIATION)
RULES, 2005.

I. The Petitioner has filed this petition against the Respondent under Section 13 (1)
(i-a) (i-b) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 for the relief of dissolution of his marriage with the respondent.
II. The aforesaid petition was referred to mediation for resolving the dispute between the parties.
In the course of Mediation, the parties along with their respective advocates participated in the mediation and

that the parties have resolved their dispute and have agreed to the following terms and conditions:
1. The petitioner and the respondent are Hindus by religion.

Their marriage was solemnized on 15.02.2019 at the residence of bride, House No.256, V V Nagar,
Vasanthpur, Bengaluru 560 061 as per Hindu rites and customs.

Subsequently the said marriage was registered on 09.10.2019 before the Registrar of Marriage,
Bagalkot vide Marriage Registration Number: BGK-HM250-2019- 2020 and stored in CD Number: BGKM13.
2.

The petitioner and the respondent state and admit that due to irreconcilable differences and incompatibility of temperaments, they did not have any compatible marital relationship between them and they are separated since May 2020.

There is absolutely no chance of a reunion between them, without reference to the allegations in the petition the parties agree that their marriage be Sri Sangamesh vs The State Of Karnataka on 30 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35229643/
3 dissolved by a decree of divorce.
3. The petitioner and the respondent state that they have a son born to them from their wedlock by name NC: 2024:KHC:45847 Hardhik aged about 4 years.

sentences.text: Presently under the care and custody of the respondent/mother and continues to be so for which the petitioner/father has no objection.

The petitioner/father is at liberty to visit the child once in a week on Sundays in between 2:00PM and 5:00PM till the child attain 7 years and thereafter from 11:00AM and 5:00PM at convenient place for both the parties with the prior intimation to the respondent/mother.
4. The petitioner and the respondent have agreed that they have no claims of maintenance/permanent alimony against each other as both are independently capable of maintaining themselves.

5. The petitioner has agreed to pay a sum of Rs. 14,00,000/- (Rupees Fourteen Lakhs Only) towards maintenance, education, medical and other incidental expenses for the child, the petitioner is paying a sum of Rs.10,00,000/- (Rupees Ten Lakhs Only) in the name of the child Hardhik by way of demand draft bearing No. 681635 dated 29.08.2024 drawn on State Bank of India, Gottigere Branch, Bengaluru and the same shall be handed over to the respondent before this Hon'ble Court while reporting settlement.

Further the petitioner has agreed to pay balance a sum of Rs.4,00,000/-
(Rupees Four Lakhs Only) to the respondent by way of demand draft bearing No. 681636 dated 29.08.2024 drawn on State Bank of India, Gottigere Branch, Bengaluru and the same shall be handed over to the respondent before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in a criminal petition intended to be filed by the petitioner.
6.

The respondent has lodged a complaint before East Zone Women Police Station, Shivajinagar,
Bengaluru against the petitioner and his family member for the offence punishable under section 498A of and 34 of IPC read with section 3 & 4 DP Act., the same in Crime No.0084/2023 pending on the file of VI ACJM., Bengaluru, in view of settlement arrived herein the respondent has agreed to co-operate with the petitioner and his family members for closure/disposal/quashing of aforesaid Crime No.0084/2023.
7.

III. In view of the aforesaid agreement entered into between the parties, the parties pray that this Hon'ble Court be pleased to dissolve the marriage solemnized on 15.02.2019 at the residence of bride, House No.256, V V Nagar, Vasanthpur, Bengaluru 560 061 and for cancellation of marriage certificate registered on 09.10.2019 before the Registrar of Marriage, Bagalkot vide Marriage Registration Number: BGK-HM250- 2019- 2020 and stored in CD Number: BGKM13 by granting a decree of divorce in terms of the agreement.

stands quashed, qua the petitioners.
